pure-announcement.rationale: It is an educational newsletter surveying agentic engineering concepts, not a launch, release note or funding announcement (its embedded sponsor ads are incidental).

duplicate.rationale: Existing concepts like agent-skills-format cover single slices of this survey, but no nearest concept covers its span of loop mechanics, state, orchestration, guardrails and observability.

unfalsifiable.rationale: Key claims are anchored to primary sources — the ReAct paper, SkillsBench and context-rot studies on arXiv, and named public tools a reader can inspect.

durability.rationale: Its substance is tool-agnostic mechanisms — the think/act/observe loop, context rot from attention dilution, state placement, subagent compression, layered guardrails, trace/replay — which will hold in twelve months even as its illustrative tool names and benchmark figures go stale.

actionability.rationale: It prescribes concrete build decisions — sub-100-line config files, deny-lists plus pre-tool hooks, a four-layer pre-commit stack, a minimum JSONL logging set, and an adoption order — that directly change how someone sets up agents.

atomicity.rationale: It deliberately bundles thirty separable concepts across six layers — context rot, prompt-injection defense, structural linting, agent loops, tracing and more — each of which could stand alone as its own note.
